title: 73. Numeracy & Number Systems: Integer Intervals and Endpoint Inclusion
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.learningObjective: Identify inclusion of endpoints in interval notation.
questions.question: Which interval includes both endpoints?
questions.explanation: In interval notation, square brackets indicate that an endpoint is included. The interval \([3,7]\) includes both \(3\) and \(7\), while \((3,7)\) excludes both endpoints. Therefore, \([3,7]\) includes both endpoints.
questions.hint: Compare the notation at each endpoint with the definition of an open or closed interval.

questions.learningObjective: Identify exclusion of endpoints in interval notation.
questions.question: Which interval excludes both endpoints?
questions.explanation: In interval notation, parentheses indicate that an endpoint is excluded. The interval \((-2,4)\) excludes both \(-2\) and \(4\), while \([-2,4]\) includes both endpoints. Therefore, \((-2,4)\) excludes both endpoints.
questions.hint: Compare the notation at each endpoint with the definition of an open or closed interval.

questions.concept: Counting Integer Elements in a Closed Interval
questions.learningObjective: Count integer elements in a closed interval.
questions.question: How many integers are in the interval \([2,6]\)?
questions.explanation: The interval \([2,6]\) includes both endpoints, so the integers are \(2\), \(3\), \(4\), \(5\), \(6\). Counting them gives \(5\) integers. Therefore, there are \(5\) integers in \([2,6]\). The alternative omits one included endpoint.
questions.hint: List every integer from the left endpoint to the right endpoint, including both endpoints.

questions.concept: Counting Integer Elements in a Half-Open Interval
questions.learningObjective: Count integer elements in a half-open interval.
questions.question: How many integers are in the interval \((2,6]\)?
questions.explanation: The interval \((2,6]\) excludes \(2\) and includes \(6\). The integers are \(3\), \(4\), \(5\), \(6\). Counting them gives \(4\) integers. Therefore, there are \(4\) integers in \((2,6]\). The alternative excludes the included right endpoint as well.
questions.hint: Look at the symbol at each end of the interval to decide whether that endpoint is counted.

questions.concept: Counting Integer Elements in an Open Interval
questions.learningObjective: Count integer elements in an open interval.
questions.question: How many integers are in the interval \((-3,2)\)?
questions.explanation: The interval \((-3,2)\) excludes both endpoints. The integers strictly between \(-3\) and \(2\) are \(-2\), \(-1\), \(0\), \(1\). Counting them gives \(4\) integers. Therefore, there are \(4\) integers in \((-3,2)\). The alternative includes one of the excluded endpoints.
questions.hint: List the integers strictly between the two endpoints, excluding both endpoints.

questions.learningObjective: Translate a two-sided inequality with mixed endpoint inclusion into interval notation.
questions.question: Which interval represents \(-1 \le x < 3\)?
questions.explanation: The inequality \(-1 \le x < 3\) includes \(-1\) because of the symbol \({\le}\), and excludes \(3\) because of the symbol \({<}\). Therefore, the interval is \([-1,3)\). The alternative excludes the lower endpoint even though its inequality permits equality.
questions.hint: Use a bracket for \({\le}\) or \({\ge}\), and a parenthesis for \({<}\) or \({>}\).

questions.learningObjective: Determine membership of an integer using interval endpoints.
questions.question: Which interval contains the integer \(-2\)?
questions.explanation: The interval \((-5,-2)\) excludes \(-2\), so \(-2\) is not in that interval. The interval \([-5,-2]\) includes \(-2\) because the right endpoint has a square bracket. Therefore, \([-5,-2]\) contains \(-2\).
questions.hint: Check whether the endpoint \(-2\) is included by the type of bracket used.

questions.concept: Listing Integer Solutions from an Inequality
questions.learningObjective: List all integer solutions of a two-sided inequality.
questions.question: Which set lists all integer solutions of \(-2 < x \le 2\)?
questions.explanation: The inequality \(-2 < x \le 2\) excludes \(-2\) and includes \(2\). The integers satisfying it are \(-1\), \(0\), \(1\), \(2\). Therefore, the solution set is \(\{-1,0,1,2\}\). The alternative includes the left endpoint even though its inequality is strict.
questions.hint: Check each inequality symbol to decide whether the number next to it is itself a solution.

questions.concept: Counting Integers in Intervals with Different Endpoint Inclusion
questions.learningObjective: Compare integer counts in intervals with different endpoint inclusion.
questions.question: Which interval contains exactly \(4\) integers?
questions.explanation: The interval \([1,3]\) contains \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), which is \(3\) integers. The interval \((1,5]\) excludes \(1\) and includes \(5\), so it contains \(2\), \(3\), \(4\), \(5\), which is \(4\) integers. Therefore, \((1,5]\) contains exactly \(4\) integers.
questions.hint: Count the integers in each interval, paying attention to which endpoints are included.

questions.learningObjective: Count the integer elements shared by two intervals.
questions.question: How many integers are in the intersection of \([-2,4)\) and \((0,5]\)?
questions.explanation: The integers in \([-2,4)\) are \(-2\), \(-1\), \(0\), \(1\), \(2\), \(3\). The integers in \((0,5]\) are \(1\), \(2\), \(3\), \(4\), \(5\). The common integers are \(1\), \(2\), \(3\). Counting them gives \(3\) integers. Therefore, the intersection contains \(3\) integers. The alternative includes \(4\), which is excluded from the first interval.
questions.hint: List the integers in each interval separately, then find the common integers.
